builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Skeleton Coding: Program Structure as a Specification for Agents
summary: The method replaces the practice of providing only end-to-end behavioral specifications (tests, input-output examples) to a coding agent with jointly specifying the program structure (decomposition into data types, modules, functions) in a high-level, code-like skeleton format alongside those behavioral tests. The cost is the upfront developer effort to design and write the structural skeleton, shifting some design responsibility from the agent back to the developer, rather than additional compute, memory, or latency overhead. Adoption can fail if the developer-specified skeleton is flawed or too rigid, as the agent is then constrained to a suboptimal structure that may not align with the requirements or may hinder its ability to find a correct implementation within that class.
rationale: This technique requires no additional GPU, cluster, or model training, and directly addresses a core production challenge of steering coding agents effectively with limited specification effort, while also reducing implementation cost and the performance gap between small and large models.
technique: Skeleton Coding: structural specification for coding agents

claims.statement: The method replaces the practice of providing only end-to-end behavioral specifications (tests, input-output examples) to a coding agent with jointly specifying the program structure (decomposition into data types, modules, functions) in a high-level, code-like skeleton format alongside those behavioral tests. The cost is the upfront developer effort to design and write the structural skeleton, shifting some design responsibility from the agent back to the developer, rather than additional compute, memory, or latency overhead. Adoption can fail if the developer-specified skeleton is flawed or too rigid, as the agent is then constrained to a suboptimal structure that may not align with the requirements or may hinder its ability to find a correct implementation within that class.

Best-performing skeleton specifications reduce mean test error by 48.4% relative to best end-to-end behavioral specifications; narrow the average gap between small and large models by about 52.4% while lowering implementation cost by 15–26x; reduce code erosion by 24.7% on average.
